headline: Geopolitical Pause Lifts Asia, Oil Slides Into Monday Open
body_html:
Monday's pre-market tone is decidedly risk-on as Asian shares and bonds bounced overnight following a weekend ceasefire of sorts between the United States and Iran. Oil prices dropped sharply on the news, providing a broad tailwind for equities even as crude markets signal they are pricing genuine adaptability rather than durable peace. The dollar retreated in tandem, while gold advanced more than one percent as investors hedged against the possibility that the pause proves temporary and a Federal Reserve decision looms later in the week.

Friday's session offered a mixed but mostly constructive backdrop heading into the new week. Homebuilders led all sectors with a gain of 2.8%, followed by Software at 2.06%. The advance-decline picture was constructive across the roughly 500-name universe, with 300 issues finishing higher against 198 lower. Semiconductors were the notable exception, the group shedding 5.09% as MaxLinear plunged 21.5% and several connectivity and memory names followed lower.

At the open, traders will be watching oil's trajectory, any further diplomatic signals out of Tehran and Washington, and whether Friday's semiconductor weakness extends or stabilizes. Red Sea shipping disruptions following a Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia add a residual geopolitical premium that could reassert itself quickly should the US-Iran pause unravel.

briefs.headline: Oil Retreats as US-Iran Fighting Goes on Pause
briefs.body: Crude futures fell markedly after the United States and Iran stepped back from active hostilities over the weekend. Analysts caution that oil markets are pricing in flexibility rather than a lasting resolution, and any breakdown in diplomatic momentum could quickly reverse the overnight drop.

briefs.headline: Gold Advances as Safe-Haven Demand Persists Ahead of Fed
briefs.body: Bullion climbed more than one percent overnight as investors balanced relief over the Iran ceasefire against lingering uncertainty. With a Federal Reserve policy decision on the calendar this week, traders are reluctant to abandon haven positions entirely, keeping gold bid even as risk appetite improves.

briefs.headline: Asian Equities and Bonds Rally on Easing Middle East Tensions
briefs.body: Shares and sovereign debt across Asian markets moved higher overnight as the US-Iran pause triggered a broad unwinding of geopolitical risk premiums. The Indian rupee was on course for its sharpest weekly advance in three weeks, buoyed largely by the pullback in oil import costs.

briefs.headline: Red Sea Disruptions Add Complexity to Oil's Overnight Drop
briefs.body: Shipping traffic through the Red Sea slowed after a Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia, complicating the otherwise bearish crude narrative. The incident is a reminder that regional instability extends beyond the US-Iran axis, and freight and energy markets will monitor the corridor closely in coming sessions.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor Sector Absorbs Heavy Blow Heading Into New Week
briefs.body: The semiconductor group shed more than five percent on Friday, the sharpest sector loss in our universe. MaxLinear fell over 21%, Sandisk dropped nearly 11%, and Credo Technology lost close to ten percent, leaving the group technically bruised as the new week begins and investors assess whether earnings revisions will follow.

briefs.headline: Schlumberger Surges to Lead Energy-Services Despite Sector Weakness
briefs.body: In a striking divergence, Schlumberger surged more than eleven percent on Friday even as the broader energy sector finished modestly lower. The oilfield-services giant's outsized gain stood apart from the tape, drawing attention to company-specific catalysts at a moment when macro oil pressures were pushing most energy names down.
